name: GLOSS_PREDICTION_TESTS
description: Three testable predictions from crazy-expert gloss analysis. Tests whether atom-level semantic hypotheses yield novel structural findings.
source: Crazy-expert agent analysis of Tier 4 gloss/etymology tables

P6.name: n-terminal MIDDLEs at Mode A/B boundaries
P6.prediction: n-terminal MIDDLEs (aiin, iin, ain) enriched at suffix mode transition lines

details.interpretation: n-terminal MIDDLEs are DEPLETED at mode transitions. They concentrate in stable mode regions, consistent with n as steady-state/continuation marker.

P6.reason: Confirms existing gloss interpretation (n = sustain/iterate) but inverts the prediction direction. Not a novel structural finding.

P7.name: o-initial MIDDLEs enriched in AZC apparatus vocabulary
P7.prediction: o-initial MIDDLEs disproportionately present in AZC (apparatus classification layer)

details.interpretation: o-initial MIDDLEs are 1.9x enriched in AZC vs Currier B. Within B, words shared with AZC have higher o-initial rates than B-exclusive words. Section C (structurally closest to AZC) has highest B-internal rate. Smooth gradient from apparatus layer to execution layer.

P8.name: f-atoms enriched in REGIME_3

details.interpretation: f-atoms ARE non-uniformly distributed across regimes (significant), but peak in REGIME_4 and REGIME_2, not REGIME_3. The smaller specialized regimes have higher f-rates. REGIME_1 has lowest (0.62%).

P8.reason: Distribution is significant but prediction direction was wrong. f-atom regime specificity may reflect general small-regime vocabulary effect rather than f-specific semantics.

summary.crazy_expert_overall_scorecard: 6 confirmed, 1 inverted, 1 wrong direction out of 8 predictions
